title: matching-in-salesforce.html
content: When {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s register for your {{variable.Object_Event}} and their information matches an existing {{variable.Object_Contact}} , {{variable.Object_Lead}} , {{variable.Object_PersonAccount}} , or {{variable.Object_Account}} the settings below will control if a record is created, ignored, etc. Relationship Settings IMPORTANT NOTE: The Relationship Setting is part of the Blackthorn Payments package, the user configuring the Relationship Settings logic will need a license to the Payments application. There is a field on {{variable.Object_EventSettings}} object called {{variable.Field_ETETSettings_RelatSettin}} . This field controls how {{variable.Object_Contact}} s, {{variable.Object_Account}} s, and {{variable.Object_Lead}} s are created and can be defined differently for each {{variable.Object_EventSettings}} you have in your organization. We recommend using the Standard Salesforce Matching and Duplication rules to prevent any duplicate records from being created. But custom, duplicate matching rules for Account, Contact, and Lead records are supported. Default Setting We provide a default Relationship Setting that your team can use. {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_RelationRule}} = "Create a New Record if No Match" {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_CreateRule}} = "Contact" {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_MatchRecords}} = "Contact" When this is configured correctly, a registration will result in an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record that is related to an existing {{variable.Object_Contact}} if there is a match or a new {{variable.Object_Contact}} if there isn't a match. Matching Logic Sequence When matching an {{variable.Object_Account}} / {{variable.Object_PersonAccount}} , you must remove "Contact" from the {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_MatchRecords}} field so the matching process can match the {{variable.Object_PersonAccount}} . The matching logic uses the following sequence. Try to fetch {{variable.Object_Contact}} s. If no {{variable.Object_Contact}} is found, then match {{variable.Object_Account}} s. And if no {{variable.Object_Account}} is found, then match {{variable.Object_Lead}} s (if selected). Updated Matching Logic An {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_LastName}} will be included in matching logic only if the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} ’s {{variable.Field_EventItem_FullName}} field is set to “Required.” This change allows use cases where matching logic identifies matches based on other available fields, such as matching only by email address. Configuration From the App Launcher, open "Relationship Settings". Click {{variable.button_new}} in the top-right hand corner. Fill in the following fields. {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_Name}} (required) {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_Default}} - if this record will be the default settings. You can only mark one Relationship Setting record as the default for your org. {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_RelationRule}} {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_MatchRecords}} - select the record type. {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_CreateRule}} - this will control which record you want configured, if you choose to create new records. You can also define a record’s {{variable.Field_Account_Type}} field’s picklist values. (The values must be a Name, not an ID.) Use the object or record’s Label name (using the API Name will cause Blackthorn Log errors). {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_AcctRecoType}} (Enter the Field Label, not the API Name.) {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_ContAcctRule}} {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_ContRecoType}} (Enter the Field Label, not the API Name.) {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_ConBucketAcc}} {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_LeadRecoType}} (Enter the Field Label, not the API Name.) Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Relationship Rules When the relationship settings match an existing record (i.e. a Contact or Lead record), it will only match and relate to the Attendee record. It won’t update the details on the matched record (i.e. the Lead or Contact record). {{variable.RelationRule_OnlyRelateMatchRe}} This setting will not create new records, but only update existing records. {{variable.RelationRule_CreateNewRecNoMat}} This settings will create a record if there is no match detected {{variable.RelationRule_AlwaysCreateRecor}} This setting will ignore duplication rules, and will create a new record even if there is already an existing record. {{variable.RelationRule_NoMatchRecCreatio}} This setting will not attempt to match or create new records. Salesforce Duplicate Rules Blackthorn's Relationship Settings harness the power of the Salesforce Duplicate Rules. You must have an active duplicate rule for any objects listed in the {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_MatchRecords}} field unless you select the relationship rule "No Matching or Record Creation." About the One Unique Attendee Email Per Event Field If the Event Settings {{variable.Field_ETSetting_1UniqAttEmail}} checkbox is checked, then the same Attendee email cannot be used for two Attendees. Each Attendee needs a unique email address. The {{variable.Field_ETSetting_1UniqAttEmail}} field on the Event Settings record provides another way to change the following scenarios. If {{variable.Field_ETSetting_1UniqAttEmail}} = “True” (checked), a warning message will be displayed when a user registers for multiple Event Items with different names but the same email address. If {{variable.Field_ETSetting_1UniqAttEmail}} = “False” (unchecked), the ERS Status will be set to “Completed" when a user registers for multiple Event Items with different names and with different email addresses. Guest Tickets For Guest Tickets that don’t collect a name and email, Salesforce sets the Guest’s {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_LastName}} to the “Primary Registrant’s {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_LastName}} + Guest + [Guest #]” and the {{variable.Field_Attendee_Email}} to the “Primary Registrant’s {{variable.Field_Attendee_Email}} ." If the {{variable.Field_ETSetting_1UniqAttEmail}} field is set to “True,” duplicate email errors will occur. To add Guest Tickets without collecting a name and email and turn off the creation of Contact records , use the Event Settings’ {{variable.Field_EVSetting_CreContGuestTi}} field. Campaigns When Attendees are added to an Event from a Campaign, the BT Event Attendee Duplicate Rule will be respected, and duplicate records will not be created. If {{variable.Field_ETSetting_1UniqAttEmail}} = "True" (checked), then all but the individual duplicate Attendee record will be processed. However, if a user clicks the Add Attendees button on a Campaign record, Attendees will be synced to the related Event even if the Event Settings’ {{variable.Field_ETSetting_1UniqAttEmail}} = “True” (checked). This will happen even if a duplicate Attendee is identified in the Attendees list. Create New Record If No Match When a primary {{variable.Object_Attendee}} registers a guest without a name for an {{variable.Object_Event}} and sets the {{variable.Object_RelationshipSettings}} {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_RelationRule}} to “Create New Record If No Match,” a guest {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record and a related {{variable.Object_Contact}} record are created. If you want to prevent the {{variable.Object_Contact}} record from being created, use the {{variable.Object_EventSettings}} {{variable.Field_EVSetting_CreContGuestTi}} (conference360__Create_Contacts_for_Guest_Tickets__c) field. The {{variable.Field_EVSetting_CreContGuestTi}} field allows Event Organizers to determine whether guest {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s' related {{variable.Object_Contact}} records will be created. When {{variable.Field_EVSetting_CreContGuestTi}} is enabled, {{variable.Object_Contact}} records are created for {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s who registered for an {{variable.Object_EventItem}} with {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_Type}} = “Guest.” If a last name and email for the guest are not provided, The guest {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_LastName}} will be the “primary {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_LastName}} + Guest [Number].” If an email is not provided for the guest, the primary {{variable.Object_Attendee}} ’s {{variable.Field_Attendee_Email}} will be used. If a last name and email are provided, a {{variable.Object_Contact}} record with those values will be created. When {{variable.Field_EVSetting_CreContGuestTi}} is disabled, a guest {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record will be created, but a {{variable.Object_Contact}} record won’t. Examples Example #1 For this example, we setup: {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_RelationRule}} = {{variable.RelationRule_CreateNewRecNoMat}} {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_CreateRule}} = "Lead" Now, when a new {{variable.Object_Attendee}} checks out of an {{variable.Object_Event}} , a {{variable.Object_Lead}} will be created. Example #2 For this example, we setup: {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_RelationRule}} = {{variable.RelationRule_CreateNewRecNoMat}} {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_CreateRule}} = "Contact" {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_ContAcctRule}} = "Bucket Account" {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_ConBucketAcc}} = "Perfect Venue" (this is an Account within our org, used for Bucket Accounts) Now, when a new {{variable.Object_Attendee}} checks out of an {{variable.Object_Event}} , a {{variable.Object_Contact}} will be created and added to the Bucket Account. Example of the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} being created. Notice the {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_Contact}} and {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_Account}} fields are populated with the information. The associated account "Perfect Venue" will have the "Bucket Account" {{variable.Object_Contact}} record added as well. Example #3 (NPSP/HEDA) For this example, we setup: {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_RelationRule}} = {{variable.RelationRule_CreateNewRecNoMat}} {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_CreateRule}} = "Account" {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_ContAcctRule}} = None Now, when a new {{variable.Object_Attendee}} checks out of an {{variable.Object_Event}} , if you're using an NPSP/HEDA Salesforce organization, the {{variable.Object_Account}} creation rules of NPSP/HEDA will apply. Person Accounts If the Person Account data model is being used, use the steps below to create a {{variable.Object_RelationshipSettings}} record for the {{variable.Object_PersonAccount}} object. In the App Launcher, enter and click “Relationship Settings”. Click {{variable.button_new}} . Enter a {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_Name}} . Select a {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_RelationRule}} . For the {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_MatchRecords}} , select “Account” and move it to the Chosen column. If a Person Account is enabled, then the "Account" option works for the Person Account. Set {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_CreateRule}} = "Account". For the {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_AcctRecoType}} field, select the value in the {{variable.Object_Account}} record's {{variable.Field_Account_Type}} field Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Matching and Duplicate Rules The BT Events Attendee Matching Rule does not use matching logic; it is a packaged rule that uses the Event_ID and runs before the ERS record processing starts. The Event_ID is used instead of the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_EventName}} to distinguish between Events with matching names. Also, the registration process will be successful if the BT Event Attendee Duplicate Rule’s {{variable.Field_AttendDupRule_ActionCrea}} is set to “Block.” Therefore, the BT Events Attendee Matching Rule fetches the existing Attendee record and updates the matching Attendee. If you disable the BT Events Attendee Matching Rule and BT Event Attendee Duplicate Rule, it will create a new Attendee record and will not perform matching. BT Event Attendee Duplicate Rule The BT Event Attendee Duplicate Rule's default setting is “Allow.” This allows for the creation of extra Attendee records without checking for duplicates. The differences between the values “Block” and “Allow” are as follows. If {{variable.Field_AttendDupRule_ActionCrea}} = ”Block,” then the Event tries to find a matching Attendee. If one is found, it will be used. If an Attendee tries to register with a duplicate first name, last name, and email, the webapp will block the registration. The Attendee will see the message: "Warning: Duplicate email registration not allowed." If {{variable.Field_AttendDupRule_ActionCrea}} = “Allow,” then a new Attendee record will be created even if a duplicate record exists. New BT Events Attendee Matching Rule With the September 2024 update to the Matching and Duplication feature, Attendees can register for multiple Events with the same name without duplicate Attendee records being created. The updated matching rule now differentiates between Events using the “Event_ID” instead of the “Event.” Old: BT Events Attendee Matching Rule The old Matching Criteria uses “(Attendee: Event EXACT MatchBlank = FALSE)." New: BT Events Attendee Matching Rule The new Matching Criteria uses “(Attendee: Event_ID EXACT MatchBlank = FALSE).” Now, the Event ID is the criteria that is used to create new Attendee records. Update the BT Event Attendee Duplicate Rule to use the new BT Events Attendee Matching Rule with Event_ID. Go to Setup. In the Quick Find box, enter and click “Duplicate Rules.” Click BT Event Attendee Duplicate Rule. Click {{variable.Button_SF_Edit}} . Scroll to the Matching Rules section. Set {{variable.Field_SF_MatchingRule}} to the new “BT Events Attendee Matching Rule.”   The Matching Criteria now shows "(Attendee: Event_ID EXACT MatchBlank = FALSE).”   Click {{variable.Button_Save}} . Now, Attendees can register for multiple Events that have the same name. Matching Logic Variations {{variable.Field_RelatSettin_MatchRecords}} There could be use cases that do not require matching on {{variable.Object_Account}} s, {{variable.Object_Contact}} s, and {{variable.Object_Lead}} s. We've added a multi-select picklist that allows users to select which object they would like to use for matching. {{variable.Field_SetAllEmailFields}} If this checkbox is enabled the matching logic will look for all email fields defined in your Salesforce matching rules from the object selected in Match Records. Then, it will match the email fields to the same value. Note: You will need to create a matching rule on each of the email address fields. Example matching rule:   Example I have the {{variable.Field_Contact_WorkEmail}} field defined on my pre-existing {{variable.Object_Contact}} record. When the {{variable.Object_Contact}} registers for an {{variable.Object_Event}} , the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} will match to the existing {{variable.Object_Contact}} using the {{variable.Field_Contact_WorkEmail}} field and then populate the {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_Contact}} field on the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} record. Duplicate Matches If there are exact duplicate matches, then the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} is matched against the most recently created record (as defined in the "Match Records" field on your Relationship Settings). If using fuzzy matching rules and multiple matches are found, then the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} is matched against the record (as defined in the "Match Records" field on your Relationship Settings) with the highest match confidence which is determined by Salesforce’s matching algorithms. If an existing {{variable.Object_CampaignMember}} is based on a {{variable.Object_Contact}} / {{variable.Object_Lead}} , then the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} will be associated with the previously mentioned {{variable.Object_CampaignMember}} . The {{variable.Field_Attendee_RegistratStatus}} for the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} and any accompanying questions will be automatically updated. Events Attendee Matching Rule The Events Attendee Matching Rule was added to prevent duplicate Attendees from being created after an Attendee registers for an Event without using an AttendeeLink. BT Events Attendee Matching Rule: If there is an existing Campaign Member based on a Contact/Lead, the Attendee will be associated with the previously mentioned Campaign Member. Matching Criteria: (Attendee: Event EXACT MatchBlank = FALSE) AND (Attendee: Email2 EXACT MatchBlank = FALSE) AND (Attendee: First_Name2 FUZZY: FIRST NAME MatchBlank = FALSE) AND (Attendee: Last_Name2 FUZZY: LAST NAME MatchBlank = FALSE) Location of Rule: Setup > Matching rules > BT Events Attendee Matching Rule
